The higher-authority business evidence supports prioritizing regulated mid-market and enterprise customers, not education startups. The quantitative segment analysis shows mid-market (28 accounts) and enterprise (9 accounts) generate 83.8% of recurring revenue, with lower churn (2.1% and 1.3% monthly) and stronger NPS (47 and 52) than SMB, while SMB churn is 4.8% and NPS is just 31 [NL-016#NL-016-S03]. The same evidence explicitly states that although the sales playbook previously highlighted education startups as high-growth, metrics prove smaller startups show weak long-term retention compared to regulated mid-market and enterprise companies [NL-016#NL-016-S03]. The leadership discussion similarly confirms the ICP is regulated mid-market and enterprise, rejecting the sales push toward SMB/edtech startups like EduVantage Labs because SMB churn is too high to support sustainable growth [NL-015#NL-015-S03].

The trade-off is that these higher-value segments require significantly longer onboarding — a median of 8.7 weeks for enterprise and 5.2 weeks for mid-market — due to permission and security complexities, and the sales cycle involves navigating enterprise security reviews rather than quick credit-card signups [NL-016#NL-016-S03]. This is in contrast to SMBs that close in under 3 weeks but churn quickly [NL-015#NL-015-S03].
